messages:
maya: FYI spotted recurring Xid 31/13 on gpu-112 (us-west-2a) during the nightly evals. node answered but pods got slow, then scheduler drained it.
lee: can you share the raw snippets you grabbed? we should make a minimal reproducible envelope for triage.
sam: agree — our current ad-hoc dumps are messy. a fixed envelope that the drain handler emits would speed root cause.
maya: pasted raw below (sanitized):
```
# dmesg (kernel ring tail)
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00:00) 31, PID 0: Graphics Xid error, pid 0: 31
[ 1234.567895] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x20:0xffffffff)
[ 1235.000012] nvidia-modeset: Unregistering GPU 0000:3b:00.0
```
```
# journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager --since "2026-03-01 02:00:00"
Mar 01 02:12:34 gpu-112 kernel: nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 01 02:12:36 gpu-112 kubelet: Pod xyz restarted due to NodeNotReady
```
```
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,uuid,driver_version,ecc.errors.volatile.device_memory --format=csv
index, name, uuid, driver_version, ecc.errors.volatile.device_memory
0, A100-SXM4-40GB, GPU-abc123, 535.65.01, 17
```

maya: Proposed minimal "gpu-failure-envelope" (to be emitted on drain + attached to incident) — small, parseable, and searchable:
```
# example payload (stringified JSON in the envelope field)
{
  "node": "gpu-112",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-01T02:12:40Z",
  "gpus": [
    {"index":"0","uuid":"GPU-abc123","name":"A100-SXM4-40GB","driver":"535.65.01","ecc_volatile": "17"}
  ],
  "dmesg_tail": "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00:00) 31, PID 0: Graphics Xid error, pid 0: 31; RmInitAdapter failed",
  "journal_snippet": "GPU has fallen off the bus; Pod xyz restarted",
  "k8s_events": "NodeNotReady, kubelet evict",
  "collect_cmds": ["dmesg | tail -n 200","journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager -n 200","nvidia-smi -q -x"]
}
```
maya: This keeps the envelope small (searchable strings) but includes commands for full dump when needed. We can base64 gzip full artifacts and add a url field.
lee: +1. two additions: include kernel version and pci ids (for vendor/slot correlation). also add `xid_code` parsed as numeric for aggregation.
sam: Also suggest mapping xid codes to our internal class: Xid 31/13 -> PCI error vs thermal vs timeout. We should ship both raw xid and mapped tag (xid_class: "memory"/"bus"/"timeout").
infra-bot: buildkite: gpu-health-agent/pipeline #452 started automatically for node gpu-112 (workflow: collect-envelope)
maya: rollout plan: implement envelope in the node-drain hook (kured/evict handler) -> ship to s3+index -> wiring in /incidents page. quick PR: add env var GPU_ENVELOPE=1 to drain job.
lee: can we get the agent to run the regex extractor locally and return a 1-line logfmt for quick searches? e.g. `gpu=node=... xid=31 ecc=17 kernel=5.15.0-...`
sam: yes — logfmt + prometheus metric (xid_count{xid=\"31\", region=\"us-west-2a\"}) will let us alert on noisy cards.
maya: next steps: I'll open a small design PR with the envelope schema + an example curl to upload. ops: can we reserve a short term tag on gpu-112 so CA doesn't reprovision it while we collect?
lee: @ops yes please hold. I'll add a reservation label: infra/preserve=gpu-112 for 24h.
sam: optional: add a small parser lambda to convert the envelope into our Xid summary table (driver, kernel, eid, xid_class) for the oncall runbook.
maya: thanks team. I'll post the PR link once ready and attach sample payloads from other recent nodes to prove variety. :thumbsup:
